name: Botox nose tip lift

card.summary: Botulinum toxin injected into the muscle that pulls the nasal tip down; a temporary, off-label tip lift with no published trials behind it.
card.aka: Nasal tip Botox, depressor septi nasi injection
card.note: Off-label use of a prescription toxin; effects are temporary and no trials were found.

quick.overview:
A Botox nose tip lift relaxes the depressor septi nasi, a small muscle that tugs the nasal tip downward. Proponents say this lets a drooping tip sit a little higher, especially when smiling.

The effect is described as temporary, lasting as long as the toxin does, usually a few months. No clinical trials of the nasal tip use were found.
quick.mechanism: Botulinum toxin blocks the signal from nerve to muscle, weakening the targeted muscle for a period of months. Weakening the depressor septi nasi reduces its downward pull on the tip.
quick.risks: Botulinum toxin is prescription-only. Reported cosmetic adverse effects include weakness of nearby muscles, headache and allergic reactions, and the FDA has issued warnings about toxin spreading beyond the injection site. The nasal use is off-label.

lead: A Botox nose tip lift is a cosmetic procedure in which botulinum toxin is injected into the depressor septi nasi, a small muscle that pulls the nasal tip and the base of the nostrils downward. Relaxing it lets the tip rest slightly higher, which people use to lift a tip that droops, particularly one that drops further when they smile or talk. It is described by proponents as a short-term, non-surgical alternative to rhinoplasty [1][2].

The depressor septi nasi originates near the upper jaw and inserts into the nasal septum and the alar part of the nasalis muscle; it also moves the nasal tip when the upper lip moves [1]. It is one of the facial muscles of the nose, alongside the procerus and nasalis [2]. Botulinum toxin products are prescription-only in the US, UK and EU, and cosmetic effects are reported to last roughly two to four months, sometimes up to six [3].

The nasal tip use is off-label: the cosmetic approval in the US concerns glabellar (frown) lines [3]. No clinical trials of nasal tip injection were located, so effect size and duration are documented as practitioner claims. In the broader non-surgical rhinoplasty field, dermal fillers are the usual tool for lifting a drooping tip or raising the bridge [4].

angle.text: People with a nose tip that dips on smiling choose this injection to lift the tip temporarily without surgery. Practitioners describe the result as subtle and fading as the toxin wears off.

paras: The depressor septi nasi pulls the nasal tip and columella downward and narrows the nostrils, acting as an antagonist to other nasal muscles [1]. Practitioners say that relaxing it reduces the downward pull so a tip that dips on smiling appears less drooped. Wikipedia's muscle entry notes only that surgeons reposition its head during rhinoplasty to help ensure normal nose position afterward and does not discuss toxin treatment [1].

Cosmetic use of botulinum toxin was first described in 1989 and the FDA approved Botox Cosmetic for glabellar lines in 2002. Smoothing generally appears within several days and peaks around one week [3]. Reported adverse effects in cosmetic use include unintended weakness of nearby muscles, headache, flu-like symptoms and allergic reactions; the FDA issued warnings in 2008 and added boxed warnings in 2009 concerning spread of toxin beyond the injection site [3].

Non-surgical rhinoplasty usually means filler injection, which can raise a flat bridge, lift a drooping tip and smooth bumps but only adds volume. Hyaluronic acid fillers last about 6 to 10 months and can be dissolved with hyaluronidase; calcium hydroxyapatite lasts about 10 to 14 months and cannot be reversed. The most serious filler risk described is accidental injection into an artery, causing skin necrosis or rarely vision loss [4]. A toxin tip lift differs in that it relaxes a muscle rather than adding volume.
The procedure appears in lists of non-surgical nose treatments as a way to lift a drooping tip without surgery, presented as a temporary adjustment that wears off as the toxin effect fades.

timeline.event: Aesthetic use of botulinum toxin first described. [3]
FDA approves Botox Cosmetic for glabellar lines. [3]
